newsitem.title: USA: ICAC sees lower world 1996/97 cotton area.
newsitem.headline: ICAC sees lower world 1996/97 cotton area.

text.p: World cotton area declined in 1996/97, even although international prices are higher than historic averages, the International Cotton Advisory Committee (ICAC) said in its monthly report.
The report estimated harvested area at 33 million hectares in 1996/97, growing to 34 million hectares in 1997/98, but down from over 35 million hectares in 1995/96.
Reductions in cotton area have occurred primarily because of competition with food crops, it said.

Even though cotton area is declining, prices will be lower in 1996/97 than in the two preceding seasons. Higher yields are expected to lead to an increase in production outside China, and China will not need to import as much cotton this year because of higher domestic stocks, the report said.
ICAC projected the 1996/97 average Cotlook A Index at 75 cents per pound, compared with 86 cents per pound in 1995/96 and a long-term average of 73 cents per pound.
The report put 1996/97 world cotton production at 88.1 million 480-pound bales (19.18 million tonnes).
Planted area in China fell to 4.4 million hectares in 1996 from 5.4 million hectares last year, the ICAC said.

The ICAC this week dropped its estimate for China's 1996/97 production to 17.0 million bales (3.7 million tonnes) from last month's estimate of 18.8 million bales (4.1 million tonnes). China produced 21.9 million bales (4.8 million tonnes) in 1995/96, ICAC said.
The China Textile Cotton Import and Export Corp said Thursday the ICAC's estimate was too low, saying China's 1996/97 cotton crop would be at least 4.35 million tonnes.
The ICAC report pegged 1996/97 world consumption at 88.7 million bales (19.30 million tonnes), up from 85.7 million bales (18.66 million tonnes) for the previous year.
World trade would be 26.3 million bales (5.73 million tonnes), down from 28.5 million bales (6.20 million tonnes.)
And 1996/97 ending stocks would be 40.4 million bales (9.19 million tonnes), down from the 40.9 million bales (8.91 million tonnes) estimated for 1995/96.
